items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: My brother, Jujus, was playing guitar. And my brother was playing bass, Sylvester. And we had a nice trio.

ctx.x: You played chords in mandolin. How did you play that? With a flat pick? Yeah.

Played lead on that. I played in mandolin. My brother, Jujus, was playing guitar. And my brother was playing bass, Sylvester. And we had a nice trio. We used to make a lot of money. We used to go around serenading people at the different hotels in Paris Christiane, Luxie, Gulfport. We used to go all around, I think. And, uh, serenading. Go from house to house. We made nice money. Sometimes we used to come back seven, five, eighty dollars. A night. We used to make nice money, I think. Oh, from drums, I wanted to…

items.title: Julius Handy Interview, 1973-05-09
items.q: I mean, when Cap was playing mandolin. When Cap was playing, we played, uh, most of the same dixie-la dance.

ctx.x: Well, how, what kind of playing did you play with your, uh, your brothers when y'all were just after three of you?
I mean, when Cap was playing mandolin. When Cap was playing, we played, uh, most of the same dixie-la dance.
Yeah, but I mean, would you play, be playing chords or would you be playing single notes picking behind him?
